title: Capital wrecks, salvage technology and automatic debris collection
status: Planned implementation requirements; not a claim of released gameplay. Published player documentation and release notes identify available features.
intent: Populate space with asteroids, capital-ship wrecks and debris; let players cut recoverable sections free, hold position beside moving wrecks, scoop loose material and use or sell recovered technology.

authoritative_control_clarification.source: Consolidated user controls: specialized module gates, target-relative hold, automatic matching-tool selection, user-triggered extraction and automatic collection.
authoritative_control_clarification.capability_gates: Mining automation requires an installed Targeting: Mining Module; ship/wreck salvage automation requires an installed Targeting: Salvage Module. Both are separately purchasable additive extensions requiring an installed targeting-computer core (Basic or higher). Advanced, Docking, Identification, Pirate or Military tier alone never grants either specialized automation. Gate target selection actions, controller engagement, automatic tool selection and automatic scoops at the authoritative runtime boundary, including keyboard and pointer paths. Mining Module alone enables asteroid/rock hold, Mining Laser selection and ore collection; Salvage Module alone enables eligible ship/wreck hold, Cutter selection and salvage/debris collection. Unrelated core targeting/docking remains usable. Missing module gives an explicit equipment requirement and does not engage the specialized controller.
authoritative_control_clarification.equipment_shop: Show Mining Module and Salvage Module as distinct indented purchasable rows under Targeting Computers, alongside the existing Basic, Advanced, Docking, Identification, Pirate and Military options. Display individual right-aligned price/status, prerequisites, Installed and exact capability description. Preserve additive modules when upgrading the core tier; buying one must not replace or imply the other. Fuel Scoops, Mining Laser and Salvage Cutter remain separately visible equipment prerequisites. Ownership comes from a successful purchase/recovery/explicit grant, not merely visiting the shop or selecting a target. XYZZY explicitly grants both modules by default and saves them as installed equipment. Every purchase also obeys the family/feature-branch prerequisite graph; recovered compatible fitting is a separate provenance-aware action.
authoritative_control_clarification.automatic_tool_selection: After the targeting computer has completed the approach and established a stable safe target-relative hold, automatically select the fitted Salvage Cutter for a ship/wreck salvage target, or the fitted Mining Laser for an asteroid/rock target. Do this on the hold-established transition, not on every frame or before the approach is complete. Show and voice the selected tool. Selection alone does not fire; the player activates the selected tool, which also automatically enables fitted Fuel Scoops to collect its released salvage/ore. Small single-scoop debris remains approach-and-collect with no cutter/mining selection or firing required.
authoritative_control_clarification.tool_compatibility: Use actual physical target classification, not hull-name string matching. Ships/wrecks select Cutter; asteroids/rocks select Mining Laser. Retain lawful/protected salvage eligibility before enabling cutting. Missing or inaccessible tools produce an explicit requirement and preserve a safe hold without substituting a combat laser or firing one. Select a supported installed mining facing and establish the corresponding safe aim/work pose; a specialized Mining fitting retained alongside Naval lasers must be genuinely usable. Manual tool override is not overwritten every frame; a newly established hold on a new target reevaluates the automatic choice. Keep the four combat laser installations and separate cutter utility fit intact.
authoritative_control_clarification.large_target: Selecting a large salvage target locks it as the primary target and automatically approaches a safe target-relative work position, then matches its drift and spin. Hold this position/orbit continuously while the target exists, including when cutting is not active, when a section is depleted and while debris is being collected. Only user cancel/manual takeover/new primary target, actual target disappearance or an explained safety interruption ends the hold.
authoritative_control_clarification.cut_and_collect: When the user activates the Salvage Cutter on the large target, fitted Fuel Scoops automatically enter collection mode at the same time. Collect released debris continuously as part of the hold; no second scoop key, pod targeting step or separate Auto salvage confirmation is required. Do not retarget the parent wreck to each fragment. Cutter release stops cutting but retains the parent lock and hold, and already reachable debris can finish collection.
authoritative_control_clarification.physical_collection: Coordinate the working offset, section selection and safe local correction manoeuvres so released debris enters the actual scoop capture zone while retaining the large-target hold. No teleporting cargo into inventory, unbounded tractor range or collision-producing pursuit through the wreck. If a fragment cannot be safely collected within the work envelope, retain its identity and parent lock, report the obstruction and pause cutting if needed; do not silently abandon the user's large target.
authoritative_control_clarification.small_target: Selecting a small item that fits in one scoop automatically locks it, manoeuvres the ship to a safe scoop intercept, activates fitted Fuel Scoops and collects it. No cutter or second activation/confirmation is required. Successful collection completes this one-item approach and reports the item collected rather than Target lost.
authoritative_control_clarification.classification: Use actual recoverable payload bounds/mass and scoop compatibility to distinguish single-scoop items from large attached salvage. Show the chosen mode immediately: SALVAGE HOLD or AUTO SCOOP. A large hull is not a one-scoop item merely because its rendered preview is small.
authoritative_control_clarification.equipment_and_capacity: The matching Mining or Salvage targeting module and fitted scoops provide their respective automation; the cutter is needed for attached ship sections, and a usable Mining Laser for asteroid extraction. Automatic activation does not grant missing equipment or bypass capacity, protected cargo or safety rules. Generic loose salvage/debris uses the Salvage Module; loose ore supports collection through the Mining Module without requiring the Salvage Module too. Refused collection leaves the item in space and gives a clear reason.
additional_acceptance: Lock a large rotating/drifting wreck, release all controls and observe stable safe hold before, during and after cutting; detached fragment recovery never changes primary target.
Activate only the cutter: scoops automatically collect reachable released material without a second input; release cutter and hold remains engaged.
Select a single-scoop item: approach, scoop activation and collection complete with no further input; the cutter is not required or fired.
Full hold, missing scoops, unsafe fragment position and target disappearance produce the correct reason and preserve finite loot, with no false Target lost after successful collection.

Establish hold on a ship/wreck: fitted cutter becomes selected automatically; establish hold on an asteroid/rock: usable fitted Mining Laser becomes selected automatically. Neither transition fires. Activating the selected tool starts cutting/mining with automatic scoop collection. Missing tool is reported without fallback combat fire or damage to protected targets.

Basic through Military core without add-on modules cannot engage specialized mining/salvage automation. Mining-only, Salvage-only and both-installed cases enable exactly their documented target modes through keyboard and pointer. Shop purchase, core upgrade, ship exchange and save/load preserve each independent entitlement.

tuning_notice: All prices, limits, percentages, ranges and rarity below are initial balancing choices and must be checked against actual native physics, equipment and economy. Money amounts here are credits; Commander stores tenths.

catalogue_findings.observation: Current main has only nine entries without a game performance profile; most are stations/platforms/special mission objects, while many large ships already have flyable refits. Salvage eligibility must therefore be independent of the presence of a game profile.
requirements: Audit all capital/carrier/large encounter hulls, including those the user cannot currently fly. Give every eligible hull a salvage profile and spawnable derelict representation using its actual showroom mesh, scale, family colours and details.
Non-flyable carrier/platform/factory objects may have abandoned variants. An active main station, protected mission object or occupied lawful capital ship is not automatically abandoned salvage.

Derelicts can be found in deep space, old battle sites and near mining regions. Seed placement and salvage content per galaxy/system/site; expose discovered sites on the existing navigation/scanner. Do not place every hull at every system.
Asteroid fields from G2 remain mandatory ordinary gameplay, with visible navigation beacons and accessible safe planet-to-star placement. Salvage does not replace mining.

equipment.name: Targeting: Mining Module
equipment.purpose: Asteroid/rock scanning, safe automatic approach and motion-matched hold, fitted Mining Laser selection and automatic scoop collection of released ore.
equipment.fitting: Separately purchased additive targeting-computer extension requiring a Basic-or-higher core. It does not grant ship/wreck salvage or require the Salvage Module for its own ore collection. Mining Laser is required for extraction and Fuel Scoops for collection; missing hardware is clearly reported.
equipment.xyzzymode: Explicitly fitted and enabled by default, independently from the Salvage Module.

equipment.name: Salvage Cutter
equipment.purpose: Utility cutter for freeing structural sections and delicate technology; Fuel Scoops recover the detached material.
equipment.fitting: Separate forward utility tool, preserving the four existing laser fittings. Select Combat Laser / Mining Laser / Salvage Cutter explicitly; only the selected tool fires. Show the utility fitting in equipment/status/showroom comparison and transferred ship fit. Do not silently replace Naval lasers in XYZZY.
equipment.mechanics: Maximum initial range 300 native units, 5 energy/second and 2 heat units/second while cutting; integrate heat/energy using the same simulation clock and existing resource model. Stop on overheat, insufficient energy or loss of valid line of sight. Cutter is not an efficient combat laser.
equipment.xyzzymode: Fitted and enabled by default with other granted equipment; existing heat/energy cheats remain separate.

equipment.name: Targeting: Salvage Module
equipment.purpose: Scan wreck sections, select recoverable systems, match drift/spin, maintain a safe working position and plan collection approaches.
equipment.fitting: Separately purchased additive extension to an existing Basic-or-higher targeting computer, not a seventh mutually exclusive tier. Preserve all Basic/Advanced/Docking/Identification/Pirate/Military capabilities and station docking. Enables ship/wreck salvage and generic debris collection, independently of the Mining Module. Requires fitted Fuel Scoops for automatic collection; cutter required only to detach attached salvage. Military tier alone does not grant this extension.

target_and_control.selection: Extend the existing R targeting action to eligible debris, inactive scoopable drones, ore pods, asteroids, wrecks and wreck sections according to installed modules. Preserve front-view-first then nearest ordering. Provide explicit target-type filters (All / Ships / Mining / Salvage) so specialized objects do not make combat cycling unusable. Selecting scoopable debris starts collection only with its matching module and scoops; selecting a wreck or asteroid starts the corresponding approach/station keeping only with that installed module.
target_and_control.fallback: Without the matching Mining/Salvage module, ordinary core targeting retains its existing capabilities and manual scoop/mining/cutting remain usable with their fitted tools. Show the missing equipment requirement instead of pretending specialized autopilot is engaged. No tier-based or UI-only bypass.
station_keeping: Hold a stable target-relative work position, matching the wreck's translational velocity and angular motion at the chosen section. Use local section position and surface orientation to aim at the cutting point.

Use the true hull/section bounds for standoff and collision checks, not distance to the craft's centre. Initial hull clearance is max(120 native units, 2 player hull radii), with the work surface inside cutter range. If geometry makes this impossible, explain why and choose another accessible section.

Implement actual bounded manoeuvring including lateral translation where required; no teleport, pose snap or hidden removal of obstacles. Thruster acceleration/velocity authority and energy demand must be explicit in ship/runtime data. Refuse unsafe or physically unattainable holds.

The station-keeping controller retains the exact wreck target while it exists, even when a section is detached or its pod is temporarily collected. A child collection target must not replace the persistent parent wreck identity.

Match spin only within the ship's manoeuvring limits; never attempt an approach through rotating protrusions. Predict swept bounds and safe entry/exit trajectories. If spin/drift is too fast, stay outside and report the limitation.

When a wreck has no recoverable sections left, mark it depleted and show 'Salvage complete'. Keep it selectable while it remains physically present; a valid hold may continue until cancelled. If it is destroyed, report destruction; if actually gone, report loss.
debris_collection: Plan a collision-free intercept using debris velocity, then place the collectible below the forward nose through the existing scoop capture volume with low relative speed (initial maximum 15 native units/second, tune to native capture physics). Do not aim straight at its centre and ram it.

Any selected space debris is evaluated: loose cargo, technology, detached modules, ore, disabled drones and empty escape pods. Collect what the actual scoop aperture/cargo bay supports. For oversized attached objects, hold and cut them into manageable pieces; explain intact payload incompatibility.

If scoops are absent, the hold is full, cargo is reserved or the item exceeds physical compatibility, keep it in space and report the reason. Reserve/check cargo space again at transfer time; never delete or silently sell the item.

After a one-off loose item is collected, stop safely and report collected rather than target lost. During large-wreck work, collect reachable released pods within the safe work envelope while continuously maintaining the same parent target and relative hold. No child retarget, separate scoop/session confirmation or departure from the parent hold is required.

Occupied escape capsules use rescue/mission passenger custody rules through the mission owner; they must not become spare equipment or alien artefacts. Empty serviceable pods are recoverable spare equipment.
target_and_control.player_control: Manual flight input, Q disengage, selecting another primary target or explicit Cancel immediately ends automatic approach/hold. Pause and information screens follow existing physical-time policy. Never auto-fire the cutter merely because a target was selected: the player activates the cutter; that same action automatically enables fitted scoops during large-target salvage, with no separate collection/session confirmation. Incoming attack interrupts cutting and warns; do not silently re-engage while the player is taking control.
target_and_control.world_time: Space remains live during approach/hold/cutting: pirates, police, missiles, heat and collisions continue. Reuse the existing freeze behaviour only when a menu already freezes simulation.
target_and_control.station_priority: Selecting an active station still invokes existing authorized docking, not cutting or a scoop approach. Non-abandoned lawful ships remain combat/normal targets; deliberate salvage damage is an attributed attack under G1 crime rules.

wreck_and_extraction.sections: Give capital wrecks several persistent recoverable sections: hull plating, cargo areas, computers, drive, weapons, shields, missile magazine, hardpoints and empty escape-pod bays. Section identity, transform, integrity, scan knowledge, progress and extracted lots are authoritative runtime state.
wreck_and_extraction.large_items: Large sections can be worked in place without fitting the entire section in the hold. Cutter frees smaller raw-material pods and named recoverable component crates; some intact modules remain too large for a small ship. Show item mass/size and needed cargo space before cutting. Cutter progress can pause/resume without resetting loot.
wreck_and_extraction.quality: Salvage Cutter preserves technology; Mining Laser yields bulk minerals/alloys from appropriate structural wreck sections but destroys delicate electronics; combat lasers/bombs generally damage or destroy valuable components. Use separate cutting work from ordinary ship hit points.
wreck_and_extraction.initial_work_time: A standard section requires roughly 10-30 uninterrupted physical seconds; large/rare systems longer. Selection, range, alignment, line of sight, heat and tool availability gate progress. Do not demand pixel-perfect timing.
wreck_and_extraction.yield: Finite seeded section yields with recognizable hull/faction provenance; high-end capital and alien wrecks can carry rarer technology. Scanning reveals item category, compatibility and a recoverability estimate without rerolling contents.
wreck_and_extraction.identity: Add a persistent WreckIdentity keyed by galaxy/system/site/spawn lineage, independent of physical ActorIdentity visit. Stable section and lot IDs extend the G1/G2 payload contract. Convert destroyed active ships to finite wrecks once through the attributed destruction pipeline; do not duplicate cargo or mission rewards already settled.
wreck_and_extraction.persistence: Persist section work/depletion, issued component lots, pending debris and collection/application/sale receipts atomically. Leaving/revisiting, target switching, resource culling, save/load, failed save and retry cannot reset loot or duplicate upgrades. Parent wreck lock uses a persisted wreck reference with current live actor resolution.
wreck_and_extraction.law_and_hazards: Show Abandoned / Claimed / Occupied / Mission protected before cutting. Respect G1 lawful self-defence, ownership and police rules; do not classify a ship as lawful salvage merely because it is hostile or non-flyable. Use bounded sparks/rotation/power-leak hazards with clear HUD feedback, not unavoidable instant death.

technology.inventory: Separate stored salvage/equipment from trade commodities and fitted equipment. Each recovered item has stable ID, category, quality, origin, mass/size, compatibility, base value and condition. Show kept components under a Salvage hold section; keep mounted lasers out of cargo-only lists.
technology.actions: Compatible ordinary salvaged upgrades can be fitted immediately after recovery, including in space, through an explicit Fit now / Store choice and the salvage inventory. Station docking is not a general requirement. Items can instead be retained or sold at a suitable station. Show exact before/after statistics, newly added features, affected mount/system and compatibility. Fitting uses one authoritative atomic transaction and does not auto-apply merely on scooping. Research is optional for explicitly marked research-only components. Alien conversion/fittings and special weapons/missiles use the PLUGH workshop rule below.
technology.future_equipment: Explicit blueprint/research discoveries may belong to commander knowledge; fitted computer/drive/shield/weapon stat upgrades belong to their actual component or hull instance. Store uninstalled items for future compatible equipment. Ship exchange transfers compatible removable instances explicitly and preserves hull-bound changes with their hull; no free duplication of permanent effects.
technology.quality_and_caps: Initial upgrade qualities may provide +5/+10/+15 percent on a declared compatible axis, subject to final balance data. Apply origin-based finite deltas with exactly-once receipts, preserve cumulative progress and promote actual components against authoritative grade templates. Use per-family/per-grade limits and a finite terminal envelope, not a 30-percent lifetime cap that prevents progression. Do not compound effects again on load.

categories.name: Computer technology
categories.uses: Random compatible ready-to-fit navigation/targeting feature modules or equipment upgrades, including scanning/acquisition/automation improvements and the next existing supported tier. Some explicitly labelled research components may also be retained for optional research recipes. Never remove current higher capabilities. Navigation remains constrained by its declared maximum and actual fuel. Recovered Mining/Salvage modules enable automation only after explicitly fitted.

categories.name: Drive technology
categories.uses: Choose maximum speed, acceleration, hyperspace spool efficiency or drive jump efficiency/reach. Separate jump reach from fuel storage. Initial fuel-efficiency improvements lower fuel cost up to the quality cap; reach improvements stay within the installed navigation computer's declared limit. Recalculate route feasibility/fuel rings and show the effective range; older 7/14/21 navigation limits do not silently disappear.

categories.name: Laser technology
categories.uses: Choose damage/power or reduced energy/heat demand for a specified compatible laser mount. Update actual firing mechanics, HUD/target specs and comparison; preserve Mining Laser/Cutter specialization. Naval/capital grants and mission-specific shield factors remain correct.

categories.name: Shield technology
categories.uses: Compatible capacity/recharge/feature improvements follow the Basic through Elite monotonic shield templates and actual component progression. Preserve saved strength, Advanced II reward provenance and current charge fraction; repeated fitting cannot heal for free. Use canonical module names, not obsolete laser-named player labels.

categories.name: Recovered missile
categories.uses: Typed serviceable missiles: standard, guided, heavy or ECM-resistant variants, with displayed damage, turning, range, blast/heat and ECM response. Initial relative choices: guided improves turning 25 percent; heavy increases damage 50 percent with speed reduced 20 percent; ECM-resistant can survive one ECM field activation then loses protection. Use real finite ammo/slot counts, clear icons, attributed combat and existing military return-fire policy.

categories.name: Laser hardpoint assembly
categories.uses: One installation unlocks one previously absent Front/Left/Right/Rear mount only where the hull's separately declared structural retrofit mask allows it. Do not add a fifth generic facing or turn a hull mask into permission for any fitting. Cobra Mk III already has all four facings and reports no further facing slots; retain/sell incompatible assemblies.

categories.name: Missile pylon assembly
categories.uses: Add one pylon within a separately declared per-hull structural limit, with an initial maximum of two above stock and the engine's verified finite hard cap. Each new pylon starts empty; update loadout, trade transfer, HUD and saves. No unlimited mounting by repeated salvage.

categories.name: Spare escape pod
categories.uses: Recover an empty serviceable pod as a stored consumable. Fit one active pod; initially allow two spares if physical storage/cargo space permits. Escape consumes one fitted pod exactly once; a spare can be fitted later. Occupied rescue capsules never count as spares.

categories.name: Alien technology / artefact
categories.uses: Take alien artefacts to PLUGH for compatible alien fittings and special new weapons/missiles, or explicitly sell them. This is now an authorized playable feature rather than a future-only placeholder. Ordinary compatible salvaged human upgrades can be fitted immediately on recovery. Use stable seeded value/condition and atomic fit/sale/workshop receipts; no reroll through repeated inspection.

source_weighted_random_salvage.source: User clarification: random upgrades/items may add features or improve equipment, and the source object's role/legal status biases the recovered goods. This section overrides any conflicting generic technology reward assumptions.
source_weighted_random_salvage.generation: Use a dedicated deterministic salvage RNG stream. Roll finite contents per stable wreck/section/lot identity at creation and persist the results, including empty/failed yields, item quality, condition and feature modifiers. Inspection, cutting, retargeting, culling, revisiting and save/load never reroll. Cargo derives from the original manifest where available; generate only missing contents using role/system/legal context. No copied manifest plus duplicate random replacement loot.
source_weighted_random_salvage.item_model: Loot can be trade cargo, ready-to-fit equipment, feature add-on modules, statistical equipment upgrades, missiles, compatible hardpoints/pylons, spare empty pods or alien artefacts. An upgrade record specifies exact effect, quality, compatibility, provenance, condition, mass/size, legality and sale value. Fit or sell is the player's choice, with no mandatory research step for a usable item. Ownership in the hold does not imply installation.
source_weighted_random_salvage.initial_weights_notice: The following percentages are starting design weights per eligible reward roll, not canon or final economy tuning. Preserve source biases if playtesting changes the exact values. Use explicit role/profile tags rather than guessing from display names.

profiles.detail: Usually narcotics or other explicitly illegal salvage goods; carry commodity/provenance legality into inventory, authority checks and sales. Illegality must be visible before collection when scanned.
Bias toward laser power/efficiency, actual missile variants, compatible hardpoint or pylon assemblies and weapon systems. Fit rules and finite ammunition still apply.

Broad random cargo, with occasional computer/drive/weapon/shield or utility items. Active main stations and protected mission stations retain ownership/crime restrictions and are not automatically salvageable.
Mostly bulk Minerals with the existing finite metal/Alloys/rare precious yield rules; do not put a generic ship-upgrade roll in every ordinary asteroid.
Mining-associated structure yields mostly raw materials and occasionally a ship upgrade. Distinguish the hermit structure/profile from a normal rock; respect occupied/protected hermits.

Use the ship's manifest first, then role/economy/legal-status weighted missing cargo. Clean traders favour legitimate cargo; offenders/fugitives have higher contraband probability. A wanted label alone neither makes every item illegal nor grants lawful salvage title.
Bias technology toward shield capacity/recharge upgrades; retain variety in computer/drive/weapon and equipment finds. Mandatory finite bounds and hull compatibility still apply.

Recover alien artefacts that can be sold or taken to PLUGH for actual compatible alien fittings and special weapons/missiles. The latest user instruction promotes PLUGH alien fitting into the current implementation scope.

source_weighted_random_salvage.overlap_resolution: Choose the most specific source profile first: Thargoid, drug factory, weapons platform, rock hermit, abandoned station, capital warship, commercial trader/cargo/carrier, ordinary asteroid. Explicitly tagged commercial carriers use their cargo profile; capital military carriers use the capital profile. No name-only classification and no double roll from overlapping classes.
source_weighted_random_salvage.legal_status_weighting: For generated commercial cargo without a saved manifest, initial contraband probability within the cargo pool is 5 percent for Clean, 35 percent for Offender and 60 percent for Fugitive, with system market availability and source role also respected. Preserve actual manifest contents regardless of those fallback weights. Distinguish commodity illegality, stolen/claimed provenance and the source ship's legal status. Use G1 authority/ownership rules, not automatic clean-kill permission.
source_weighted_random_salvage.value_and_progression: Roll useful but bounded quality and compatibility from source tech/role, with rare high-end finds. Source-weighted finds may add supported features (for example a targeting add-on or equipment capability) as well as percentage improvements. Reuse fitting caps, structural masks and baseline-based upgrade limits; no arbitrary unlimited module stacks or free duplication on ship exchange.
source_weighted_random_salvage.presentation: Show source, item/category, legal warning, exact new feature/stat effect, fit compatibility and sale value in the salvage target scan/hold and station Fit/Sell UI. Update targeting/salvage player docs with source biases and explain that contents vary; never promise a guaranteed shield/weapon drop.
acceptance: Seeded distribution samples preserve each role bias and overlap priority, including capital military versus commercial carrier and hermit versus ordinary rock.
Saved source manifests and legal context are retained; clean/offender/fugitive fallback cargo distributions differ without classifying all wanted cargo as illegal.
A random recovered module can be fitted for an actual new feature or equipment improvement, or sold instead; unfitted hold ownership never enables targeting automation.
Repeated inspection/cut/reload/revisit/failure/retry does not change rolled item, quality, condition, modifiers, value or depleted state.

Thargoid salvage produces artefacts; PLUGH offers actual compatible alien fitting and special weapons/missiles. Ordinary recovered compatible upgrades can be fitted immediately in space; alien workshop requirements remain explicit.

recovery_fitting_and_plugh.source: User instruction on 2026-10-15: alien artefacts taken to PLUGH permit alien artefact and new weapon/missile fittings; upgrades can be fitted when salvaged. Supersedes earlier station-only fitting and future-only alien upgrade wording.
recovery_fitting_and_plugh.immediate_ordinary_fitting: After collecting a compatible ordinary ship upgrade/item, offer Fit now / Store; also expose Fit from salvage inventory while in space. No compulsory station visit or research recipe. Fit requires a supported slot, matching equipment, finite capacity and no contradictory protected transaction. Show exact effects and any replacement, retain replaced recoverable equipment where space permits, and refuse safely otherwise. Selection does not silently fit random loot.
recovery_fitting_and_plugh.plugh_workshop: Each galaxy's existing secret PLUGH station exposes an Alien Fittings service when docked. Identify PLUGH by authoritative system identity/flag. Held alien artefacts unlock compatible alien artefact fittings and the special weapon/missile catalogue. Show actual effects, slots, compatibility, artefact requirements and any credit/service cost before explicit Fit/Exchange. Use finite, data-defined recipes; consume or install the selected artefact/item exactly once only after successful validation. Keep Sell/Store as alternatives and preserve finite credits.
recovery_fitting_and_plugh.real_effects: Workshop results must be real equipped systems/weapons/typed missile ammunition, not cosmetic inventory labels. Define damage/energy/heat/tracking/ECM/shield or other feature effects in authoritative equipment data, and update actual combat, loadout/HUD and comparisons. Existing upgrade caps, structural mount/pylon masks, navigation/fuel limits and missile capacity still apply. Do not advertise an option that has no runtime implementation.
recovery_fitting_and_plugh.presentation: Recovery HUD/voice names the item and offers fitting when compatible. PLUGH services explain alien conversion versus ordinary immediate fitting. Update targeting, salvage, equipment and PLUGH player documentation, marking these features pending only until the integrated feature ships.
recovery_fitting_and_plugh.validation: Fit an ordinary salvaged upgrade in space and observe its real effect; store/sell instead; reject incompatible/full replacements without losing items. At PLUGH fit an artefact system and obtain/use special weapon or missile with correct finite costs/capacity. Outside PLUGH the specialized workshop is unavailable. Save/load/failure/retry preserves items, effects, costs and exactly-once receipts; fitting/unfitting cannot heal shields or clone ammunition.

presentation.hud: Fixed small font at every size: SALVAGE target/section, distance/clearance, relative speed, spin mismatch, Hold/Approach/Blocked status, cutter work/heat and required/free cargo capacity. Retain enlarged central scanner and compact side data.
presentation.target_panel: Use the existing zoomed model panel: hull name, abandoned/claimed state, rotation, section list, remaining salvage and discovered technology. Highlight accessible section on the shaded actual hull. Show compatibility requirements before extraction/application.
presentation.voice: Existing shared text/voice event queue: 'Salvage target acquired', 'Matching drift', 'Position matched', 'Section released', '<item> recovered', 'Cargo hold full', 'Unsafe approach', 'Salvage complete'. Announce transitions once, suppress per-frame repetition. Honour voice preference.
presentation.equipment_and_market: Show cutter under Mining and Salvage; independent Mining/Salvage modules beneath the single Targeting Computer with existing named core modules. Recovery offers Fit now/Store for compatible ordinary upgrades, including in space. PLUGH has the alien fitting workshop; station services offer Inspect/Fit/Sell and explicit optional research recipes. Show exact stat/feature changes, compatibility, prerequisite locks and right-aligned finite costs.

player_documentation.requirement: Provide detailed targeting-computer and add-on player documentation, linked from README, with matching in-game help and equipment-shop descriptions.
coverage: Capability comparison for the Basic, Advanced, Docking, Identification, Pirate and Military targeting modules; actual prices, tech availability, full purchase prerequisites and inherited versus separately purchased capabilities.
Independent Mining Module and Salvage Module purchase/installation, exact capabilities and separate core/tool/Fuel Scoops requirements. Military alone does not grant either extension.

Controls and examples for asteroid/rock hold and automatic Mining Laser selection; ship/wreck drift/spin hold and automatic Cutter selection; continuous automatic scoop collection when the user activates the selected tool; one-scoop automatic debris approach/collection.
Persistent parent wreck lock, tool-selection versus firing, cancellation/manual takeover, full hold, unsafe approach, missing equipment, ownership/protected targets and no-fire rules.
ID/Pirate/Military target information, origin/destination, ECM and military return-fire according to actual implemented behaviour.
XYZZY grants, saved installation state, core upgrades and ship/module transfer; costs and limits derived from authoritative data rather than stale duplicated numbers.

Stat-based component promotion, seven-grade shields, standard Basic navigation/energy with Intermediate/Advanced modules, immediate compatible fitting in space, PLUGH alien fittings and separate acquisition/purchase provenance.
player_documentation.acceptance: Include a readable capability table and worked mining, large-wreck and loose-item examples. Clearly label pending versus shipped behaviour until the real feature lands, then reconcile documentation against the integrated tested controls and equipment. Coder2 supplies G2 rules/evidence; no competing README edits.

targeting_module_presentation.source: User requests changes to Equip Ship and the command screen; interpret command screen as Commander Status, consistent with existing commander/equipment displays.
targeting_module_presentation.model: Present one Targeting Computer with named add-on modules, rather than a flat list suggesting several complete targeting computers. Basic, Advanced, Docking, Identification, Pirate and Military appear as feature modules alongside the independent Mining and Salvage modules.
targeting_module_presentation.equip_ship: Use one Targeting Computer heading with indented Basic, Advanced, Docking, Identification, Pirate, Military, Mining and Salvage Module rows. Show right-aligned price/status, full prerequisite-purchase locks and exact capability/dependency descriptions. Core and specialist branch prerequisites come from one graph, not row order. Preserve existing prices unless another explicit equipment balance rule changes them.
targeting_module_presentation.commander_status: Replace the single TARGETING: MILITARY-style summary with Targeting Computer status and an indented installed-module/capability list, including Mining and Salvage independently. Show inherited capabilities honestly, for example Enabled via Military Module; do not invent separate paid purchases for lower capabilities or imply the two specialist modules are inherited from Military. All installed modules must remain reachable by scrolling at compact sizes.
targeting_module_presentation.compatibility: Existing highest-tier saves preserve their exact capabilities and equipment entitlement through normalization/label mapping. The internal tier accessor can remain for compatibility. Module display, shop checks, actual runtime gates and documentation must agree. Navigation computers are unaffected by this presentation change.
